sites.name: Humanities Building
sites.blurb: Start where West Campus teaching began.
facts: Humanities was one of the first academic buildings ready when the Stony Brook campus opened in 1962.
In the earliest days, most classes met here while the campus was still under construction.

sites.name: 9/11 Memorial Arch
sites.blurb: Pause at a campus memorial tied to Humanities.
facts: The Memorial Arch near the Humanities Building was donated by the Stony Brook Alumni Association.
It honors Stony Brook alumni lost on September 11, 2001.

sites.name: Frey Hall
sites.blurb: Claim a transformed original science building.
facts: The Chemistry Building was among the first academic structures of the 1962 West Campus.
After renovation into a classroom building, it was renamed Frey Hall.

sites.name: Academic Mall Fountain
sites.blurb: Stand in the redesigned heart of campus.
facts: The Academic Mall was redesigned into a greener gathering spine with fountains and water features.
The project expressed a ‘heart of the campus’ vision for everyday student life.

sites.name: Student Activities Center
sites.blurb: Log the student-life hub of the academic core.
facts: The SAC concentrates dining, events, and student activity on the main campus walk.

sites.name: Stony Brook Union
sites.blurb: Claim a historic center of student community.
facts: The Union has long anchored student life on West Campus.
Campus lore also remembers the old pedestrian bridge connections involving the Union and Library.

sites.name: Staller Center for the Arts
sites.blurb: Mark the arts stage of West Campus.
facts: The fine arts complex opened in phases in the 1970s.
It was renamed the Staller Center for the Arts in 1988 following a major gift.

sites.name: Charles B. Wang Center
sites.blurb: Arrive at a cultural threshold on campus.
facts: The Charles B. Wang Center opened in 2002 as an Asian cultural center.
Its design includes garden courts, water, and a distinctive tower silhouette.

sites.name: Frank Melville Jr. Memorial Library
sites.blurb: Log the knowledge heart of West Campus.
facts: The original library on this campus opened in 1963.
It is named for Frank Melville Jr., father of benefactor Ward Melville.
A major expansion wrapped new wings around the original modular structure.

sites.name: Zebra Path
sites.blurb: Walk a student-made stripe of campus art.
facts: The Zebra Path was created in 1981 by student Kim Hardiman as public art.
It connects the Academic Mall area with northern campus routes.

sites.name: Jacob K. Javits Lecture Center
sites.blurb: Pin a high-traffic lecture landmark for new students.
facts: Javits is a major lecture hub on the academic campus walk.

sites.name: Earth and Space Sciences
sites.blurb: Claim a cornerstone of the science quad.
facts: Science buildings on West Campus historically hosted branch libraries and research teaching spaces.

sites.name: Physics Building
sites.blurb: Mark physics on your campus run.
facts: Physics facilities are part of the core science identity of Stony Brook.

sites.name: Mathematics Tower
sites.blurb: Add the math complex to your map memory.
facts: Confirm the public-facing building label and best entrance pin on site before enabling.

sites.name: Light Engineering
sites.blurb: Orient yourself in the engineering quad.
facts: Engineering facilities expanded as Stony Brook grew from its early science-and-engineering mandate.

sites.name: Computer Science
sites.blurb: Pin CS on the main-campus mental map.
facts: Verify the exact building name and entrance students use day-to-day.

sites.name: Life Sciences Building
sites.blurb: Claim the life sciences complex.
facts: Life Sciences anchors biological teaching and research on West Campus.

sites.name: Wolfie Statue
sites.blurb: Meet the Seawolf in bronze.
facts: The Wolfie statue is a popular meeting landmark and symbol of Seawolf identity.

sites.name: SBU Landmark Letters
sites.blurb: Claim the letters that spell campus pride.
facts: The SBU letters near the Union area are a photo-friendly orientation landmark.

sites.name: Glacial Boulders
sites.blurb: Find ice-age stone woven into campus culture.
facts: Hundreds of glacial boulders were unearthed during campus construction and kept in the landscape.
Painted rock traditions are regulated—permission is required.

sites.name: Bridge to Nowhere Echo
sites.blurb: Unlock a memory of a vanished campus bridge.
facts: The unfinished-then-completed pedestrian bridge became campus lore as the Bridge to Nowhere.
It was later demolished; this node is interpretive—place it only where a responsible public pin exists.
sites.notes: Enable only after choosing a respectful public standing point

sites.name: Roth Quad
sites.blurb: Learn a major residential quad on foot.
facts: Roth Quad is one of the key residential neighborhoods students navigate daily.

sites.name: Tabler Quad
sites.blurb: Orient around Tabler’s loop.
facts: Tabler’s circular paths are a classic wayfinding landmark for residential life.

sites.name: West Side Dining
sites.blurb: Pin the west-side dining landmark.
facts: West Side Dining anchors everyday life for nearby residential communities.

sites.name: Ashley Schiff Preserve
sites.blurb: Touch the wooded preserve named for a beloved professor.
facts: Ashley Schiff Preserve honors political science professor and naturalist Ashley Schiff.
The woodland was set aside as a memorial landscape on campus.

sites.name: Paul Simons Memorial Bike Path
sites.blurb: Claim an access point on the campus loop path.
facts: The Paul Simons Memorial Bike Path loops the wooded campus for bikes, runs, and rollers.

sites.name: Administration Building
sites.blurb: Know where campus administration lives.
facts: The Administration Building is a practical orientation pin for services and official campus business.
